reconciliation_notes:
Both verifiers returned trust=high and recommended GOLD, but I set the twin to SILVER per the AUTHORING-SPEC tiering rule (twin grade = lowest load-bearing BW/peak/capacity field). Reasoning:

AGREED / KEPT (both verifiers confirm): hbm_capacity_bytes (288 GiB = 309,237,645,312 B exact, GiB convention), hbm_bandwidth_bps (8 TB/s), infinity_cache_capacity (256 MB), onchip_sram_capacity (40 MiB LDS = 160 KB/CU x 256), device peaks BF16 2.5 PF dense / FP8 5.0 PF dense / FP64 78.6 TF, compute_instances 256 CU, clock 2.4 GHz, TDP 1400 W, process node N3P(XCD)/N6(IOD). These are all GOLD directly from AMD datasheet/whitepaper with third-party cross-checks.

DISPUTED -> downgraded + documented:
1. hbm_energy_pj_per_byte (5.0/6.0): both verifiers flag AMD publishes no per-byte HBM energy. Kept the estimate (H100 7 pJ/B anchor x ~30% HBM3e gain) but BRONZE. Energy is NOT in the spec's load-bearing set (BW/peak/capacity), so it does not by itself force a lower twin tier; marked directional-only in the twin's energy_note.
2. infinity_cache_bw_bps (1.7e13): both verifiers dispute (unpublished, extrapolated from MI300 LLC). Kept as BRONZE estimate. To avoid a single unpublished cache bandwidth dragging the whole twin to BRONZE, the Infinity Cache is annotated as an AUXILIARY cache tier, NOT the primary reuse tier — the experiment blocks GEMM into LDS. This is documented in the level note.
3. onchip_sram_bw_bps (1.57e14): verifier-1 agrees SILVER, verifier-2 disputes (derived). Reconciled as SILVER (derived from published 256 B/clk/CU) — this IS the primary reuse-tier bandwidth and IS load-bearing.

WHY SILVER (not GOLD): the primary load-bearing chain the experiment uses is HBM (backing) -> LDS (reuse) -> MXU (compute). HBM BW/cap = GOLD, device peak = GOLD, but the reuse-tier bandwidth (LDS 1.57e14) and per-instance MAC (4.9152e12) are DERIVED (SILVER), and matrix_unit is a representative CDNA4 shape (SILVER). Lowest load-bearing = SILVER, so twin = SILVER. No load-bearing field is BRONZE (the two BRONZE fields — HBM energy and Infinity Cache BW — are auxiliary), so the twin does not fall to BRONZE.

matrix_unit resolution: verifier called [16,16,32] an FP8 MFMA tile, but it is equally the CDNA4 BF16/FP16 MFMA shape (K doubled from CDNA3's 16x16x16). Since peak_macs_per_s describes the BF16 path, dtype_bytes=2 is internally consistent with matrix_unit [16,16,32].

Sanity: per_instance_mac_s (4.9152e12) x 256 CU x 2 = 2.516e15 FLOP/s ~ 2.5 PFLOPS dense BF16, matches datasheet. Order-of-magnitude vs H100 anchor: HBM BW 2.4x, device peak 2.5x, LDS >> H100 SMEM aggregate — all same order or expected generational uplift. JSON validated (single-accelerator nested chain, RB-05).
unresolved: hbm_energy_pj_per_byte: AMD publishes no per-byte HBM energy; 5.0 read / 6.0 write remain unverifiable BRONZE estimates (H100 anchor x HBM3e efficiency gain).
infinity_cache_bw_bps: 1.7e13 unpublished by AMD; BRONZE estimate from MI300-gen LLC order. Disputed by both verifiers; treated as non-load-bearing auxiliary tier.
l2_bandwidth_bps (1.0e13) and infinity_cache line_bytes: not separately published; used H100-class order-of-magnitude anchors.

matrix_unit shape: [16,16,32] is a representative CDNA4 MFMA tile; CDNA4 also exposes 32x32x64 and scaled FP8 variants — the single canonical shape for this twin's BF16 path is a modeling choice (SILVER).
